articleTitle: The Influence of First Local Escillator Spectrum on the Dynamic Range of HF Communication Receiver
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The sensitivity, immunity to interference and maximum noise to signal ratio of firat local escillator of HF communication receiver are directly influenced by its signal's spectrum and power. In this report the influence af the first local escillator's signal on basic characteristice of the receiver are discussed and the way of designing the linear channel for maximum dynamic range is shows.

articleTitle: Passing the Undesired Oscillations of an Oscillator Through the Waveguide Transmission Line Elements
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transformation of wave modes and the filtering effect on the discontinuties of the multimode fider transmission line have been investigated experimentally. Sixteen different types of discontinuties, formed by such waveguide elements, as E-bend, H-bend, E-plane T, H-plane T, directional couplers of different types, non-mutual waveguide elements, etc. have been studied. The analysis of the experimental results permits the requirements to the filters for the undesired oscillations suppression to be defined more precisely.

articleTitle: The Front-to-Back Ratio of the Antennas for Radio Relay Links and Methods of its Improvement
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the main characteristics studied in the analysis of the EMC is the front-to back-ratio of antenna. Main factors are considered which influence this ratio. The main results of theoretical study are given and various methods and devices for improving the front-to-back ratio are analyzed. The experimental results for various antenna types are listed. On the basis of the analysis specific measures for improving the front-to-back /side/ ratio are given.

articleTitle: Assessment of a Batch of Radio-Interference Producing Electrical Appliances on the Basis of an Extrembly Limited Sample
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Distribution of radio interference level probabilities are investigated, which are accepted when assessing a batch of electrical appliances according to the CISPR method. The boundary conditions of assessment of a batch by means of a sample are determined when the producer's and consumer's risks are equal to each other.

articleTitle: On the Relationships Between the Quasipeak and Effective Values of Quasi-Impulsive Processes of Man-Made Radio Interference
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Report presents expressions and graphs of dependence of detection coefficients of inertial detectors on average repetition rates of interference pulses in pulse trains, a standard deviation of their amplitudes and parameters of radio interference measuring sets. Expressions are determined and graphs presented for relationships between quasi-peak and effective values of interference measured by CISPR measuring sets.

articleTitle: On the Estimation of the Geostationary Orbit Capacity Limits
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A problem of the estimation of the geostationary orbit capacity limit with regard to natural interfereneces only is put forward and solved. The analysis is carriad out for analogue FDM-FM And digital PSK communication systems and the Unit is evaluated in tenas of potential capasity of communication channels. Some basic approaches to a further increase of the geostationary orbit capacity are discussed.

articleTitle: Methods to Improve EMC in TV Broadcasting
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper some methods are discussed which allow for better use of frequency channels and better quality of reception. The following may be considered as basic steps towards this end: - Introduction of operating conditions for TV transmitters which allow for lower protection ratios - improving the immunity of TV receivers - use of orthogonal polarisations for TV stations which interfere with each other - improving EMC of terrestrial and satellite TV systems by establishing the protection ratio for terrestrial TV from the satellite TV, taking into account statistical characteristics of wanted and unwanted signals - use of statistical methods for TV network planning, based on real equipment characteristics; this allows for lower requirements on the planning stage, without lowering the reception quality. The paper quotes results of experimental investigations on the methods mentioned above and gives their qualitative evaluation.

articleTitle: Probability Characteristics of RFI to Mobile Surface Radio Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The evaluation of interference situation is made using the system of amplitude, temporal, spatial and frequency statistical characteristics. The system of statistical characteristics is described, based on the results of experimental research of electromagnetic interference from automobile electrical equipment on routes.

articleTitle: Radio Interference Compensation in Angular Modulation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Frequency modulation FM systems, which are used in Radio-relay, tropespheric and satellite communication, in UHF broadcasting, in mobile communication systems and so on, are commonly applied in communication technique. Due to sharp growth of the operating system number in all the frequency ranges, new reception method development which permits to separate effectively several different FM signals, occupying common frequency band, is very actual. The results of study channel and multichannel noise compensator efficiency for FM signals are given in the report. The problems of such noise compensator technical realization for a multichannel communication system are considered. The technique for computation of efficiency suppression interference in FM receivers is suggested. It is shown in the report that noise compensator application permits to double FM communication system capacity without broadening the occupied frequency band.

articleTitle: The Spectrum Calculation of the Out-of-Band Radiation of an Impulse Magntron
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The spectrum calculation of the out-of-band radiation of an impulse magnetron has been made on the basis of the impulse shape and the frequency-magnetron current curve (the pulling figure curve). The obtained results have been compared with the spectra, measured by virtue of the spectrum analyzer. The up-to-date methods and measuring facilities have been shown to permit the initial data for the Spectrum calculation with the error of the order of ±6.0 dB (on the levels minus 20 ÷ 60 db) to be obtained. Some regularities, which should be taken into account during optimization the behavior of a magnetron, have been determined.

articleTitle: Determination of Interrelation Between Arbitrary Radiators by Means of Series Expansion in Multipole Fields
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Report discusses a method of determination of interrelation between arbitrary radiating electrodynamic systems by presentation of radiation fields of each system in the form of series expansion in Tectorial spherical wave harmonics. The expressions for active and reactive components of mutual impedance are obtained. A solution of a problem of determining an interrelation between two col-linear vibrator radiators is given.

articleTitle: Determination of a Criterion for a Degree of Electromagnetic Compatibility of a Complex Consisting of Interference Sources and Receptors
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A criterion is proposed for assessment of a degree of electromagnetic compatibility of a complex consisting of a finite number of interference sources and receptors.

articleTitle: A Noiseproof Meter of Noise Signal Intensity Measurement
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present report gives algorithms of processing of an additive mixture of a normal noise signal and pulse noise with apriori unknown distribution of its parameters. The functional diagram of the meter and results of investigations are presented.

articleTitle: Radiation Properties of Natuaral Formations in the Millimeter Wave Range
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of an experimental research of land and atmospher radiation at frequency of 38,75GHz and 140GHz are reported. These data make it possible to evaluate scattering power by reflection from land and atmosphere influence on brightness temperature of land. Microwave emission from, grass, soil and snow have been investigated.

articleTitle: Calculation of Lightning Effects on Communication Cable
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The handbook of the CCITT on lightning protection contains approximate solutions concerning the surge current and voltage calculation when lightning discharge influences the communication cable. The paper gives a close-form solution to determine the relation path-time for the surge current and lightning voltage cable sheath/cable conductors.

articleTitle: Forecast of RFI to Mobile Surface Radio Service
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The forecast is based on the results of long year experimental research of electromagnetic interference /EMI/. The forecast of an within the range of mobile surfice radio services Is described with sone examples of its use to evaluate the reception quality of radiotelephone and discrete, information on mobile station.

articleTitle: A Magnetic-Field Generator Intended for Measuring the Immunity of Radio Electronic Equipment to Interference
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A circuit and construction of a magnetic-field generator are proposed, which guarantees a quasi-spherical hodograph of a field vector; a calculation of a field strength is given and the dimensions of the operating region of the device are determined.

articleTitle: Some Practical Aspects of Satellite Communicatios Systems Coordination
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some approaches which simaplify the coordination procedure are discussed and a new method of coordination based on specially chosen telephone channel group is proposed. The method of the determination of a coordination group is presented add the appropriate calculation examples are given.

articleTitle: EMC and Protective Measures in Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Protective measures against danger and trouble are classified and evaluated in case of outer interference /power plants, electric rail-ways, lightning, radio transmitters/. The following protective measures can be distinguished: - protective measures in conventional communication systems - protective measures in communication systems to be newly developed having a system-immanent protection. In this respect classification depends on: - communication cable - transmission technology - exchange technology. This study includes pulse-shaped interference cases. Different variants of protective measures are described and their technical parameters are compared. Criteria for selection and problems of application in case of definite measures are stated.

articleTitle: Redundancy Reduction and Picture Quality
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with possibilities of frequency spectrum limiting of television digital systems by using statistical picture features and redundancy reduction in such a way that reproduced analog picture quality doesn't decrease. The statistical measurements of picture quality were made after the frequency bandwidth of the analog television signal had been limited. The measurements were made to assign quality grades to pictures reproduced on colour television receivers as well as on monochrome television receivers.

articleTitle: Signal and Noise Spectra Superposition - A Measure of Transmission Performance
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The author's investigations have been performed in confirmation of theoretical relationship [1,2] between desired signal pollution and probability of faultless reception. Spectrum coverage ratio as a sum of products of spurious and desired signal spectrum discrete values has been proposed.

articleTitle: A Statistical Estimate of the Protective Action of the Antennas of the Radio Relay Links
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the prosese of design of the radio relay links the calculations include the median value of the protective action of the antennas. But this characteristic is not static one and because of that it is more correct to define it by probability distributions fro. which it follow. that for some time intervale the protective action is much lower than the median value. The differential law of distribution of the protective action for the radio relay link antennae has the form <tex>$\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{k}) = \int\limits_{o}^{\infty} z\mathrm{p}_4 (\mathrm{k}\mathrm{z})\mathrm{p}_2 (\mathrm{z})\mathrm{d}\mathrm{z}$</tex> where p<inf>4</inf> and p<inf>2</inf> - differential distributions of the useful signal u<inf>4</inf> and noise u<inf>2</inf>. Integral law is obtained as <tex>$\mathrm{w}(\mathrm{k}) = \int\limits_{o}^{k} \mathrm{p}(\mathrm{k})\mathrm{d}\mathrm{k}$</tex> Examples are given for calculation of the protective action distributions for the antennas of direct sight links and tropospheric relay links. For the tropospheric case the equation of the integral distribution has the form <tex>$\mathrm{w}(\mathrm{k}) = 4/(\mathrm{k}^2 + 4)$</tex>. The loss in the protective action of antennae is defined as <tex>$\Delta \mathrm{k}_{\text{db}} = 10 \ell g (4/\Delta\mathrm{T}-4)$</tex>. Calculation according to this formula for intervals of time ΔT =20%, 0.5% and 0.05% /i.e. for intervale in which, according to the CCIR recommendations, noise in telephone channels is standardised/ defines the loss of the antenna protective action for 6, 23 and 33 dB respectively.

articleTitle: ZIR - The New Program for Interference Computation in Radio Link Network
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the most important problems in radio link network planning is the electromagnetic compatibility. The paper presents a method and a general description of the computer program for calculation of common channel interferences caused by other radio links at the input of a given radio link receiver and their influence on the quality parameters of channels at the output of the radio link. As distinct from previous programs /OZIR, ZIHA/, ZIH - program enables to study the radio link networks with analog systems of telephone, television and broadcast type as well as with digital systems. Moreover, it includes a number of new procedures which extend the range and improve the accuracy of calculations, do illustrate the presented method some printouts of calculations results obtained with the aid of R-32 computer are included.

articleTitle: Some Aspects of Measuring Radio Frequency Interference Generated by Static Power Converters
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) problems resulting from static power converters (SPC) are commonly known but their satisfactory solution has not yet been found. One of the reasons of this state is the fact that contemporary test methods, though in agreement with national standards and international recommendations, give unrealistic and misleading results of directly used for testing power equipment with semiconductor power converters in situ In this paper some problems concerning RFI measurements and suppresssion under real operating condition are discussed. Some recommendations for suppressing RFI generated by static power converters (SPC) are given.

articleTitle: Ground Observations of Power Line Radiation Coupled to the Ionosphere and Magnetosphere
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ground-based VLF observations show evidence that strong whistler-mode waves in the magnetosphere are often stimulated by harmonic radiation from electrical power transmission lines. These stimulated emissions sometimes dominate the wave activity in the kHz range. A VLF transmitter at Siple, Antarctica has been used to simulate these power line effects with ~0.5 W radiated power at a given frequency. Occurrence statistics of power line effects are also summarized.

articleTitle: Objective EMC Criteria for Radio Systems : Do they Exist?
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Complete presentation of the entire family of EMC criteria for radio systems is attempted. The level-spacing rules for signals and distance-spacing rules for stations are discussed. The conventional approach /in CCIR documents/ as well as advanced analyses, elaborated in the USA are outlined. The methods and the terms seem to be noncompatible with each other.

articleTitle: Polish Lightning Research - Electromagnetic Theories
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The charges of the lightning are considered as induced charges, during the downward leader and the upward return stroke. These charges of the leader are examined first for a uniform inducing field, which is the difference of the primary field E<sub>O</sub> and the resistance field E<inf>R</inf>, afterwards for a nonuniform inducing field. The irregularities of the inducing field are due chiefly to variations of E<inf>R</inf>, corresponding to the peculiarities of cold streamer and hot plasma. The discussion leads to the relaxation theory of the stepped leader. Electrodynamics of the return stroke follow. Its velocity and surge impedance are analysed.

articleTitle: Measuring LF and MF Antenna Radiation Patterns by Means of a Helicopter
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with a method of measuring power gain and radiation pattern of LF and MF antennae, applying the standard field produced by a loop antenna installed on a helicopter. A method of radionavigation necessary for this purpose has been presented. Results of measurements of several antennae have also been given.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Measuring Co-Channel Interference Among AM Broadcasting Transmitters
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The measuring requirements for determining the real service area of AM broadcasting transmitters are summarized. The present possibilities of measuring co-channel interference are described and compared. We introduce a new method called Envelope Analysis Method /EAM/ suitable for measuring co-channel interference at the presence of wanted signal. The advantages and practical limitations are given. The measuring results prove the usability of the EAM.

articleTitle: On some Probabilistic Approach to EMC Problems in Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is supposed there is a finite number of signals S<sub>o</sub>, S<sub>n</sub> in an electromagnetic enviroment. Each i-th signal is assigned by a number of parameters g<inf>i</inf>, g<inf>m</inf> and each ij-th parameter - by a corresponding probability density function f(g<sup>ij</sup>). The fractional compatibility between two signals S<sub>o</sub> and S<sub>i</sub>, with regard to J-th parameter, is /fig. 1/

articleTitle: Propagation of Electromagnetic Waves up to 40 GHz Through Sand and Dust Storm Periods
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Sand and dust storms are very frequent in desert parts of countries like Iraq, Iran, Sudan and Sahara. The optical visibility reduces to twenty meters or less under its severe conditions. Sand and dust particles absorb and scatter electromagnetic energy similar to rain drops, snow and fog. Attenuation of microwave signal up to 100 GHs is studied by Roderic et al. (l). Experimental results on attenuation of microwave signal at 10GHz in presence of sand particles have been conducted by Ahmed, (2), using open cavity resonator. Here an attempt is made to estimate attenuation of microwave signal when propagating through sand storm conditions. The concept of form factor is used to estimate scattering of energy by spherical sand particles. This approach predicts that attenuation increases faster above 10 GHz frequency. Experimental results performed over Nasiriya-Baghdad Microwave Link are given during adverse sand storm conditions.

articleTitle: The Growth and the Content of DNA and RNA of Seedlings of Pisum Sativum L. and Cucumis Sativus L. In the Environment Without Exterior Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The content of DNA increases about 31% in the shoots and 37% in the roots of seedlings of Pisum sativum cultivated in the environment without electromagnetic field of 100 kHz to 300 MHz. In the same conditions, the content of DNA increses about 41% in the shoots and 9% in the roots of Cucumis sativus. The content of RNA aggrandizes also in the seedlings cultivated in the Faraday's cabin, in comparison to the control conditions.

articleTitle: Fast Signal Fluctuations for Anomalous Long Distance SHF and UHF Propagation
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When solving EMC problems the data are needed on fast interference signal fluctuations at anomalous high levels which are observed during small percentages of time. Under such anomalous conditions of long distance radiowave propagation fast fluctuation have another character than under standard conditions /normal level of signals/. The statistical characteristics of instantaneous signal level value for anomalous propagation are given. The relation of these Characteristics with a mean value of the signal level is analyzed. The influence of the terrain conditions, climate and wavelength on fast fluctuations is analyzed too.

articleTitle: On the Uncertainty of Estimation of Conditions of Transmission Systems Equipment Operation when Checking the Interference by a Broadband Device
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Such requirements are formulated for an amplitude-frequency characteristic of a broadband device intended for check of impulsive interference, which guarantee a minimum uncertainty of estimation of conditions of transmission systems equipment operation.

articleTitle: Influence of Nonideal Bandstop Filter on Measurement Results of AM Receivers Using Spectral Method
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper a spectral method for testing of AM radio receivers is shortly reminded and results of considerations relative to question of influence of bandstop filter on measurement results of radio receivers using this method are presented. In particular the following new problems are discussed: - question of choice of bandstop filter attenuation, - influence of nonideal frequency characteristic of bandstop filter, - influence of phase shift in the circuits forming spectrum of testing signal.

articleTitle: Requirement on Instrumentation for the Statistical Measurement of the Man-Made Noise
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Various apparatuses for the statistical measurement of atmospheric radio noise have been developed up to date, most of which-however can be used direct or in a modified way for the statistical measurement of man-made noise. A number of apparatuses for the measurement of atmospheric radio noise are simply described with some explanation on a few results of measurements: those have been developed for (1) synchronous analysis of well-known four distributions and a few moments for the noise, (2) precise measurement of lots of APDs and a few moments and (3) repetition of a small time length of measurements of the threshold amplitude of very-low-probability-value for a long period of time. In the later part of the paper, a new apparatus developed for the measurement of the man-made noise in terms of both APD and CRD is simply described with some explanation of results of measurement executed for a particular man-made noise.

articleTitle: Radio Noise Level due to Electric Power Lines and its Relation with Line Design Parameters
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The main results of radio noise measurements made in Poland for 220 and 400 kV power lines are presented. The influence of various line parameters, such as conductor diameter and number, phase spacing, height of conductor above ground on the radio noise level for power lines is discussed. The basic philosophy of choosing the line parameters and line route on design stage in Poland is described taking into acrount radio noise level, electrical field gradient and corona losses.

articleTitle: Shielding and Immunity from Radio Interferences Basic Objects of Measurement Methods
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Standards on measurement methods of immunity from conducted or radiated radio interferences are particularly urgent as in many cases they have the hidden porpose of establishing limits. In order to approach this goal an analysis is carried out of the concept of immunity and basic conditions asked by measurement methods are pointed out. A detaild development of these topics with the relative theoretical analysis and mathematical developments is not possible in a short paper as the present one. Then the matter will be examined only from a general point of view, with no reference to different specific devices. Difficulties, drawbacks and lacks of principal methods at present under consideration, will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Artificial Mains-Networks Used in Measuring Man-Made Radio Interference
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the basis of analysis of radio-frequency impedances three groupa of maina are singled out, namely, those of ground means of transportation, those of airplanes and ships, and those of ground stationary objecta. A corresponding type of an artificial. Mains-network is determined for each of these groups. Two types of artificial mains-networks meet the CISPR requirements; the third type (R = 75 Ohms, L = 17µH) is not specified. A circuit diagram of a high-current artificial mains-network is given with parameters R s 50 Ohms, L = 50 mH for a frequency band of 0.01 to 30 MHz. Characteristics of this artificial mains-network are calculated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Radiation Hazards Caused by HF Equipment
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents results of measurements carried out by National Radio Inspection in Poland on workers protection against injurious effects of strong electromagnetic fields in the frequency range 0.1 - 300 MHz. On the basis of comparision of National Regulations requirements with results of field intensity measurements, evaluation of radiation hazards is given Moreover, some technical and organizational recommendations to reduce the field levels at work stands are contained.

articleTitle: EM Field Produced by Frequency-Stabilized R.F. Plastic Welders
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Most plastic welders operate in free-radiation ISM bands, The field on the fundamental frequency is then unlimited, and can be harmful to the environment. The paper gives experimental values of the field in the distance of 10 metres from such equipment and describes possibility of diminishing it by simple partial screening.

articleTitle: Propagation in Urban Areas Between Antennas of Low Elevation at VHF and UHF Frequencies
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present results of a series of short distance /20-1000m/ propagation measurements conducted in the urban area of Budapest in the VHF and UHF band in order to supplement presently available propagation data. The results of our measurements have shown, that for line of sight paths short distance propagation between antennas of low elevation in urban areas during hours of heavy road traffic does not follow the anticipated plane earth law but follows a modified free space law.

articleTitle: Noise Sources in Near-Space Spectrum Pollution
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Global monitoring of thunderstorm activity and lightning detection have important scientific and practical applications. Of several monitoring techniques, space platforms still offer considerable promise if the difficulties encountered in past rf satellite experiments can be overcome. One of the past major problems was insufficient knowledge of the near-space radio noise and interference environment from which the lightning signatures had to be extracted. In this paper, the characteristics of that environment as presently known are examined in terms of the contributing noise and interference sources, their frequency spectra and relative importance. The radiation characteristics of both natural sources, categorized as terrestrial and extraterrestrial, and man-made sources, categorized as incidental, unintentional and intentional, are considered. The effects of propagation through the atmosphere and ionosphere are described briefly as they affect the RFI environment at the satellite receiver. In considering the probable magnitudes of rf lightning signatures received at satellite altitudes compared to the RFI background, it becomes obvious that monitoring frequencies must be chosen in portions of the radio spectrum unoccupied by deliberate transmissions.

articleTitle: Assessment of Radio Interference from Power Lines Taking into Account their Fluctuations in Time and Space
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Statistical parameters of radio interference, radiated by over-head high-voltage power lines, are considered. The results of measurements which were made at individual sections of a power line are regarded as realisations of a radio interference process. The process in question is assumed to be stationary over the observation time interval. Expressions for determination of statistical parameters of radio interference are proposed.

articleTitle: The Problems of Linearity and Pulse Response in the Design of an Audio-Frequency Interference Voltmeter
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this report some design aspects of an audio-frequency interference voltmeter are presented. According to CISPR recommendations, the quasi-peak detector is the only nonlinear part of the audio-frequency interference voltmeter. An original solution for a quasi-peak detector with an extended range of correct impulse response and improved linearity through application of a nonlinear feedback, are presented. The application of an additional nonlinear element allows us to compensate for the influence of the detector diode nonlinearities. The results of measurements illustrating advantages of the discussed audio voltmeter are presented. The parameters of this voltmeter agree with CISPR Publication No 6 [3], this voltmeter may be useful as a standard meter for measurements of audio devices and radio receivers.

articleTitle: Management Techniques for Improved Spectrum Utilization
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes techniques that can be used for improved management of the radio spectrum. Emphasis is placed on the introduction of spectrum engineering techniques into the traditional spectrum management process. In particular, techniques that provide for the orderly investigation of spectrum, review of new system developments to promote electromagnetic compatibility, resolution of potential harmful interference problems, engineering measurements and monitoring, and spectrum management training are presented.

articleTitle: Test Site Suitability Assessment for Radiation Measurements. Theoretical Results
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Procedures to assess the test site suitability for radiation measurements are considered with soecial care to the TEC standard 3- metre method. The so called "site attenuation curves" are calculated and plotted for the frequency range 30 to 1000 MHz, taking into account the ground reflection, the shortening and the mutual influence of the dipoles. These curves are compared with those obtained in a more simplified way, considering far-field conditions and isolated antennas. Conclusions are drawn about the convenience of the two methods.

articleTitle: Methods and Equipment for Measuring the Pulling Figure of a Magnetron with a View to Calculating the Out-of-Band Oscillations Spectrum
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The suggested procedure (of paired pulses at constant temperatures of an anode assembly and a cathode surface) permits the static pulling figure to be measured with a satisfactory accuracy. The dynamic pulling figure has been measured by method of a mismatched high-Q resonator and by virtue of time wavemeter scheme. The difference in the values of a static and a dynamic pulling figure has not been determined to exceed the measurement mistake.

articleTitle: Frequency Assignment in Duplex Communication Systems to Avoid Intermodulation Interference
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In duplex communication systems a consideration of the power levels associated with particular sets of intermodulation products can enable the waiver of the intermodulation interference imposed constraint in the frequency assignment where such power levels are low enough to be considered insignificant. An assignment making use of such a selective procedure results in considerable spectrum saving.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Flicker Influence
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is advisable to estimate flicker by means of simulation of the source of light, of eyesight inertia and adaptation as well as human fatigue. Simulation enables us to synthesize the pattern of flickermeter and to find the transfer function of a light filter. Equivalizing between the dose of flicker and fluctuation curve is to be accomplished for all the frequencies. Not taking into account the slow adaptation lowers the flicker estimation at low frequencies. The period of fatigue accumulation from the flicker is 10 min. That is why the equivalizing of disturbances is carried out using a ten-minute flicker dose without differentiation of disturbances according to their duration and without the application of continuous integration and statistical analysers.

articleTitle: R.F. Interference Generated by a Thyristor-Controlled, Hand-Held Drill Motor
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The mechanisms which generate radio-frequency interference (RFI) in a thyristor-controlled, hand-held drill motor are described. An equivalent circuit model incorporating these mechanisms is postulated. The relative importance of the mechanisms, in terms of the interference level which they generate, is established by practical measurements after isolating the individual RFI sources so far as is practicable. It is concluded that the commutatator-brush contact resistance variation and the commutation of the armature coils are the main RFI sources. Thyristor control forms an additional source which is particularly important in association with the armature winding.

articleTitle: EMI Problems in the Design of Telephone Switching System
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In experience accumulated in the course of implementing and field testing "PROTEO” system prototypes made by Società Italiana Telecomunicazioni Siemens S.p.A. (SITS), we have found that the high switching frequencies, and the size of row of cabinets have imposed a rational integration of EMC requirements with system technical specifications. In this paper the method adopted for the above mentioned integration is outlined. The method is supported by specific environment measurements and by simulation program for time domain signal analysis.

articleTitle: An Application of Automatic Spectrum Monitoring Equipment
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes an application of automatic spectrum monitoring equipment. The application is to measure spectrum occupancy on the frequencies allocated to the land mobile services in the United States of America. The equipment and the measuring method are briefly described and examples of the measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Conceptual model of the Electromagnetic Environment for EMC Analysis of Radiocommunication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Efficient processing of a great amount of data used in EMC analysis requires the application of computerized data base technology. The content of each data base consists of information taken from elements selected of the real world and also taken from the relationships existing between them. An appropriate conceptual model is needed to arrange a data base according to all users' needs. The conceptual model presented in this paper describes the geographical and electromagnetic environment of radiocommunication systems.

articleTitle: EMI Problems in the Design of Electronic Switching Sistems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent developments in telephone switching systems using digital integrated circuits, impose reliability specifications which are not particularly aKin with previous commercial or military standards; therefore, it is mandatory to take into consideration a specific EMI environment as an essential component in design procedures. In experience accumulated in the course of. implementing and field testing “PROTEO” system prototypes made by Società Italiana di Telecomunicazioni S.p.A. (SITS), with particular relation to the central control and switching network, we found that the high switching frequencies, and the size of row of cabinets, have impose a rational integration of EMC requirements with system technical specifications. In this paper the method adopted for the above mentioned integration is outlined in its individual steps, which are analysed in relation to the following: system emission and susceptibility; internal compatibility between subsystem with reference to trading off the electrical behaviour of ground buses, power supply, buses, and signal buses, external compatibility with systems and EMI environment; noise margin characteristics of digital integra ted circuits; observance of specifications typical of telephone exchange. The method is supported by sophisticated simulation programs for time domain signal and power analysis, and measuring system for frequency domain characterization.

articleTitle: Voltage Responses of Screening Tubes to Unit Step Lightning Currents with Regard to Ferromagnetic and Non-Ferromagnetic Materials
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Between the screened conductors and the screening tube arises a longitudinal voltage u<inf>1</inf> when a partial lightning current i flows trough the tube. The worst case is given by an unit step lightning current. u<inf>1</inf> is mainly characterized by its front time T<inf>1</inf> and its maximum value û<inf>1</inf>. The knowledge of T<inf>1</inf> is of great importance both for the overvoltage analysis of a connected circuit and for the design of protective devices against the longitudinal overvoltages. For non-ferromagnetic tubes the voltage responses are independent on î. For ferromagnetic tubes there is a dependency on î corresponding to the ferromagnetic parameters of the material.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Method for Analysing VHF and UHF Interferences on Broadcast Receivers
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Here is a method presented suitable for a computer-aided analysis of interferences occurring in TV and VHF-FM broadcast receivers and due to the signals of the VHF and UHF radiotelephone transmitter-receiver equipments. The paper introduces the algorythms for seeking the interference signal components and determining their interference intensity. It sums up the programme characteristics and deals with their application.

articleTitle: Natural and Man Made Noise in the Earth-Ionosphere Cavity at Extremely Low Frequencies. (Schumann Resonances and Man-Made "Interference")
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The equations for the earth ionosphere cavity resonance fields are stated and some of the approximations used in their derivation are indicated. Typical electric and magnetic 5 to 20 Hz Schumann resonance field intensities are listed and compared with the level of other natural and man made electromagnetic noise. Applications of Schumann resonances to thunderstorm location and measurement of global lightning activity are reviewed briefly. Ionospheric conductivity profiles appropriate for this frequency range are discussed and the importance of atmospheric conductivity below 60 km is pointed out.

articleTitle: Height-Patterns of VHF Television Waves
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is very important to forecast the interference range of TV waves, due to reflection and screening by newly constructed high construction in order to establish adequate countermeasures at the planning stage. Vertical field distribution, so-called height pattern characteristics of TV waves incoming to a tall construction should be determined for this purpose. Height pattern characteristics of VHF TV waves with horizontal polarization were measured, by means of a vehicle and helicopter, in the line of sight propagation path in which the waves are reflected by the water's surface, the ground of rural or suburban areas and mountains or hills with a grazing angle of less than 3°. This report describes height pattern features, equivalent reflection coefficients of ground reflecting surfaces and differences between calculated and measured value of a free space field.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Emitted by Lightning Stroke. Theorical Model Taking into Account the Ground Conductivity. Comparison with Experimental Measurements Made at Saint Privat D'Allier
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In a precedent paper [1] we computed the electromagnetic field emitted by a lightning return stroke above a perfectly conducting ground plane. In this paper we use the same model and develop it by using a harmonic analysis to resolve the Sommerfeld integrals which represent the contribution of the finite conducting ground plane. The effect of the finite ground conductivity is presented and compared to the perfectly conducting ground case. These theoretical results are compared to the experimental measurements

articleTitle: Calculation of Terrain Distribution of Field Strength for VHF and UHF Television and Broadcasting Services
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with computer calculation of the terrain distribution of field strength in the VHF and UHF ranges. The problem is a very important one, because its solution simplifies the analysis of EMC characteristics for radio network designing. In calculation of the field strength the technical characteristics of a station, the length of the propagation path and the terrain irregularities as well as the radiometeorological conditions have been taken into account. The algorithm of the worked out program and an numerical example have been presented. The program enables to obtain directly the graphs of fixed values of the field strength.

articleTitle: Interface - EMC for Data and Signal Lines
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to assure the electromagnetic compatibility of systems, it is necessary to pay close attention to the interfaces between system components. The cause of electromagnetic induction is mainly the common-mode interference. Such interference can be avoided in shielded systems in which the equipment is totally enclosed by the shield. When balanced transmission lines are used, it is possible to operate without shielded cables if specially dimensioned interface filters are installed.

articleTitle: Model of Topographical Environment of VHF/UHF Broadcasting Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Terrain features may cause large differences in the extent of both the desired and the undesired signals, and therefore, play an important role in the planning and analysis of broadcasting systems, In the paper there are presented ways of coding a topographical map so that it can.be read into a computer. The methods presented are suitable for efficient coding and storing of terrain height, surface coverage, ground constants etc., and allow relatively quick estimation of terrain dependent propagation factors.

articleTitle: Increase of Noise Immunity in Relay Control Systems by Using on-off Element with Generalized Characteristic
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a method to increase the noise immunity in a relay control system is presented. Using on-off elements with generalized characteristic at the input of relay control system under consideration, the noise voltages will he intercepted before reaching the logic assembly.

articleTitle: Information and Documentation System for Radio-Frequency Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The philosophy of radio frequency spectrum (RFS) management as a natural resource assumes that signals of one frequency are not interfered by others and that at the same time they do not interfere some other signals. Information system for radio frequency spectrum management must secure optimum decisions in management which provides the achievement of the information system in SFR of Yugoslavia.

articleTitle: Properties of Smart EMI-Measuring Receivers
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper consists of four parts. Part 1 discusses general requirements, measuring methods and fundamental design principles for broad-and narrowband interference measuring receivers. Part 2 gives directives and possibilities for intelligent automatic interference measuring receivers and fieldstrength meters. In Part 3 a special problem is described relating to the CISPR weighting circuit: the error caused by the receiver's internal noise when measuring pulses with very low repetition frequencies will be discussed and a solution of the problem will be given. Part 4 gives some extended applications of intelligent EMI-measuring receivers.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Pulse Interference in Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of generation of pulse interference in electronic equipment arising when using pulse units - multivibrators, digital processing units and power-supply units for electronic commutators. There is shown the feasibility of the analysis of such interference with the help of well-known theoremas about opening and closing the switch on the assumption of the linearity of the equivalent coupling network of interference generator. This analysis is carried out with the substitution of the corresponding current or voltage generator for electronic commutators, and the equivalent coupling network is composed for the specified frequency band.

articleTitle: Computer Prediction of VHF/UHF Transmitting Station Coverage Area
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two methods for prediction of the coverage area of a transmitting station are presented. The first method is based on a generation of a line printer map showing the line-of-sight and shadow areas, The second method bases on a map of the signal intensity over the whole region in question, The programs elaborated, and the data base used are described, and a few examples are cited.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Guidelines for the Next 20 Years Impact of the WARC - 1979
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of the World Administrative Radio Conference, Geneva 1979 are discussed, with particular regard to its influence on future policy in the field of EMC. General guidelines concerning the investigations aiming to reduce the EMC environment pollution, and improve spectrum utilization as given in the conclusions.

articleTitle: The Improvement of Electromagnetic Compatibility Characteristics of the Marine HP and MP Radio Communication Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Consideration is given to the results of the measurements of voltage levels and E.M.F. inducted at receiving antennas by the marine transmitting systems.

articleTitle: Pulsed Radiation Teratogenic Effects
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Teratogenic effects of SHF electromagnetic fields applied to pupae of Tenebrio molitor coleopteron are reported. Pulsed microwave radia tion gave results different from those due to CW: at the same average power level pulse modulation seems to reduce teratogenic effectiveness of radiation, at least as far as nonthermal effects are concerned.

articleTitle: Millimetre Spectroscopy as a Method of Studying Microwave Radiation Influence on Biologically Active Compounds
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Attenuation of microwave (MM and SubMM ranges) was shown to reflect intermolecular interactions in solutions for water solutions of different classes compounds-bioorganic, organic and inorganic.

articleTitle: Reciprocity Relations Between Currents and Fields in Gyrotropic, Anisotropic and Bianisotropic Media
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We consider the wave fields <tex>$\underline{\tilde{\mathrm{e}}}_{\mathrm{i}}(\underline{\mathrm{r}})\equiv [\underline{\tilde{\mathrm{E}}}_{\mathrm{i}}({\mathrm{r}}), \underline{\tilde{\mathrm{H}}}_{\mathrm{i}}({\mathrm{r}})], \mathrm{i} =1,2$</tex>, generated respectively by two arbitrary current distributions <tex>$\underline{\tilde{\mathrm{J}}}_{\mathrm{i}}(\underline{\mathrm{r}})\equiv [\underline{\tilde{\mathrm{J}}}_{\mathrm{e}}(\underline{\mathrm{r}}), \underline{\tilde{\mathrm{J}}}_{\mathrm{m}}(\underline{\mathrm{r}})]$</tex>, where <tex>$\underline{\mathrm{J}}_{\mathrm{e}}$</tex> and <tex>$\underline{\mathrm{J}}_{\mathrm{m}}$</tex> are the electric and equivalent magnetic current densities. The currents and fields are immersed in media having electric and magnetic permeabilities <tex>$\underline{\underline{\varepsilon}} (\underline{\mathrm{r}})$</tex> and <tex>$\underline{\underline{\mu}} (\underline{\mathrm{r}})$</tex>, which possess a plane of symmetry, y = 0, such that <tex>$\underline{\underline{\varepsilon}} ({\mathrm{x}}, {\mathrm{y}}, {\mathrm{z}}) = \underline{\underline{\varepsilon}} (\underline{\mathrm{x}}, -{\mathrm{y}}, {\mathrm{z}})$</tex> and <tex>$\underline{\underline{\mu}} ({\mathrm{x}}, {\mathrm{y}}, {\mathrm{z}}) = \underline{\underline{\mu}} ({\mathrm{x}}, -{\mathrm{y}}, {\mathrm{z}})$</tex>. Guided by results obtained for plane-stratified media, it is shown directly from Maxwell's equations for the media (and without the need to work in Fourier <tex>$\underline{\mathrm{k}}$</tex>-space) that <tex>$\int\underline{\mathrm{e}}_1(\underline{\mathrm{r}})\cdot \underline{\mathrm{J}}_2(\underline{\mathrm{r}})\mathrm{d}^3\mathrm{r} = \int\underline{\mathrm{e}}_2'(\underline{\mathrm{r}})\cdot \underline{\mathrm{J}}_1'(\underline{\mathrm{r}}) \mathrm{d}^3\mathrm{r}$</tex> where <tex>$\underline{\mathrm{e}}_{\mathrm{i}}'(\underline{\mathrm{r}}), \mathrm{i} = 1,2$</tex>, represents the wave fields generated by <tex>$\underline{\mathrm{J}}_{\mathrm{i}}'(\underline{\mathrm{r}})$</tex>, the respective reflected current systems, i.e. reflected with respect to the plane of symmetry, y = 0. The importance of this result is that currents and fields are all measured in the same physical medium, and not in a (hypothetical) transposed medium as in Lorentz reciprocity, yielding direct applications in ionospheric propagation.

articleTitle: Measuring Tests for Shielding Effectiveness of an Enclosure of Energy Distribution Devices Used in Building Complexes
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In modern building complexes such as hospitals spacing is problematical, especially when substations and electromedical instruments are closely situated. Transformers and switching bays must be located near the examining rooms; this is due to economic operation of the power system. Despite these space limitations closely situated electromedical appliances must function reliably at all times and under all circumstances. The task is to reduce the disturbances which are caused by transformers and switching bays on the measuring instruments so that a certain limit of effect is not exceeded. For this reason the distribution substation must be situated in a ferromagnetic enclosure. The following paper is concerned with these problems occurring while testing the effectiveness of these shielding enclosures before distribution substations go into operation. Therefore transformers and bus-bars must be replaced by coils to simulate their magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Influence of the Millimetre Wave Electromagnetic Radiation on the Biological Structures and Different Organisms
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report discusses the main regularities of the intermal intensity millimetre wave radiation influence on different biological objects at the molecular, cellular levels, as well as at the level of complex leving organisms. The main investigated models are: hemoglobin and erythrocytes of human blood, bacillus E.coli, golden staphylococus, moulden fungus mice and rats. The results have shown that the millimetre wave radiation strongly influences on the biological objects development and activity, the influence beeing of a resonance character, i.e. it is observed at different frequencies with the density of irradiation power of some mW/cm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: The Robustness of the Locally Optimum Detectors for Non-Gaussian Noise
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the performance of various non-linear detection schemes are compared with the performance of the locally optimum threshold (small signal) detector, e.g., that detector which approaches true optimality as the signal vanishes. It is shown that the locally optimum nonlinearity (for a given impulsive noise situation) maintains good performance (i.e., is robust) over a wide range of different noise conditions. It is also shown that, for a wide range of non-Gaussian noise conditions, performance is degraded only slightly by using appropriate suboptimum nonlinearities (e.g., hard limiter and adaptive clipper) in place of the locally optimum nonlinearity, but that some suboptimum nonlinearities are not robust. In this paper, the Middleton models for Non-Gaussian noise environments are used.

articleTitle: The Limits for Anisotropy of the Mixture of Field-Modes to be Satisfied in the Reverberating Chambers with Variable Geometry Used for Power Measurements
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In a well designed mode-stirred reverberating chamber for power measurements have been determined experimentally, in a few typical cases, the minimun distances of the measuring point from the chamber metallic surfaces, from the openings and from the sources of energy to get validity to the proportionality between the square of any field component and the average output power of the source of energy.

articleTitle: Fluctuations of Amplitude, Intensity, Phase, Angle of Arrival and Propagation Direction of Millimeter Radiowaves in Turbulent Atmosphere
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mastering of the millimeter waves band opens large perspectives for radio communication. The principal adventage. of the millimeter waves band is its extremely wide frequency band, what makes it possible to solve the problem of EMC essentially. In this paper the results of theoretical and experimental research of the millimeter radiowaves propagation in turbulent atmosphere are reported. The experiment was performed at wavelegth of 2 mm at horizontal path of length 5,6 km and 8 km in strongly turbulent atmosphere. Fluctuations of radiowave, fundamental parameters as amplitude, intensity, phase, angle of arrival and direction of propagation have been investigated. That makes it possible to estimate a noise immunity of the millimeter communication channel in strongly turbulent atmosphere.

articleTitle: Communication Satellite Spectrum Conservation Through Advanced Technology
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The communication capacity of the geostationary orbit is analyzed as an aid to determining whether the demand for frequency assignments and orbit locations is likely to soon exceed what is available. Capacity is shown to greatly exceed any realistic projection of global needs for the foreseeable future, if effective use is made of the available technology.

articleTitle: Production of Digital Model of Topographic Map for Radio Communication Planning
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presented work describes a novel method of graphic data representation applied in computer readable fora production of topographic map. Computer readable form of topographic map shall be used for radio communication planning. The basic feature of this method is unique treatment of different map elements. There is no need for any special preparing of topographic map. The procedure for grid structure filling is also described, based on automatic modification of initial parameters. The basic information about project implementation is also supplied herein.

articleTitle: Some Techniques for Suppressing TV-Signal Interference Caused by Tall Buildings
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two problems concerning the techniques for suppressing TV-signal interference caused by tall buildings were studied: (1) Estimation of the influence of the building cross-section on the scattering characteristics. (2) Design of a periodic wall structure which produces little interference. For problem (1), we have established an economical method for calculating the electromagnetic fields scattered by a rectangular building, which can also be used in cases of other types of cross-section. Scattering patterns of rectangular and Hotel New Ootani type buildings are presented. For (2), we have got a wall structure with periodic distribution of dielectric constant which reflects only 10% of the incident energy back to the ground, in a frequency band 100 to 200 MHz.

articleTitle: Prediction of and Potential Trouble Measures Against Broadband Man-Made Radio Interference to a Scheduled System of Satellite Television Broadcasting at 12 GHz
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the basis of prescribed and calculated parameters of a 12 GHz satellite television broadcasting system (CTB 12 GHz system), CCIR materials and results of investigations made in the Leningrad Branch of Radio Research Institute the present Report predicts a probability of interfering effect of broadband interference from motor transport on receiving installations of a CTB 12 GHz system for community-antenna and individual reception. Some considerations are given concerning the measures for improvement of reliability of high-fidelity reception, especially in case of individual receiving installations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling Through the Braid of a Coaxial Cable
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The shielding effectiveness of the braid of a coaxial cable is usually characterized by the transfer impedance, inductance and capacitance. Extensive measurements have been made in time domain and then, using Fast Fourier Transform procedures, the variation in amplitude and phase angle of the transfer impedance has been obtained in the 10 kHz - 30 MHz frequency range. A comparison between theoretical and experimental values of the transfer parameters is given.

articleTitle: "Equipment Methods of Protection of Wire Intercity Trasmission Lines Against Radio Noises"
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A review is given of engineering of radio technical methods of protection of wire intercity transmission lines against radio noises. This methods decrease essentially the noise effect without a noticeable quality impairment of channel transmitting useful information. The present report gives results of a test service of operating of multichannel communications with the use of noise proof equipment based on the methods of strobing, frequency rejection, amplitude limitation and radio noise compensation. The main attention is given to the method of compensation, since its use in virtue of linearity of operations made is not associated with distortions of useful signals. As a rule, to obtain an apriori information about noises phantom chains of communications are employed. The use of radio technical methods in combination with traditional methods of protection permits to decrease noises in transmission lines up to levels close to the standards.

articleTitle: CCIR and Efficient use of the Radio-Frequency Spectrum
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A wide range of problems connected with CCIR (mainly CCIR Study Group l) activities in the field of efficient spectrum utilization and in providing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of radio equipment is discussed. General conclusions reflecting the contents of documents of the XIVth CCIR Plenary Assembly (Kyoto, June 1978), on problems concerning definition of spectrum use and efficiency, spectrum management, system and propagation models for the evaluation of EMC, technical criteria for frequency sharing, etc. are given. Further achievements resulting from a study of these questions by CCIR Special Preparatory Meeting for the WARC-79 (Geneva, October-November 1978) and by Administrations, to be presented in contributions to the Interim Meeting of CCIR Study Group 1 (Geneva, June 198C), are characterized. In particular the main provisions of the draft of Report "Spectrum management and computer aided techniques" prepared by Interim Working Party 1/2 are discussed.

articleTitle: A Computing Model and its Experimental Testing for an Evaluation of Electromagnetic Interferences Created by Interfering Circuits on Transmission or High-Voltage Lines Above a Dissipative Ground
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we shall present useful calculation for a prediction of the electromagnetic field created by interfering circuits on linear horizontal transmission line over an imperfectly conducting ground. The interfering circuits are assimilated to antennas and treated by using the dipole radiation theory. The current distribution is determinated by the transmission line theory. We present here the computational procedure allowing a fast and accurate calculation of the electromagnetic fields components of a serie of dipoles. We give the linear characteristics Z, Y of the transmission line by incorporating the ground effects. The response of a terminated one-wire transmission line set over the ground and excited by a non-uniform field is given. A comparaison between computed results given by the model and experimental measurements is provided.

articleTitle: Minicomputer Software Development for Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The ever increasing crowding of the spectrum requires that automated data bases, coordination, and EMC analysis techniques be employed to efficiently manage the spectrum. Recent reductions in cost and size, along with increases in capacity, have made the application of minicomputers cost effective for many spectrum management applications. The National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) uses a minicomputer system to implement certain spectrum management techniques.

articleTitle: A Practical Method of Calculation of the Induced Voltage
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The lightning current discharging through a down conductor can produce induced voltage in near open loops. The calculation method of the induced voltage is well known [2, 4], but other formulas have to be worked out for each arrangement. A practical method has been developed to calculate the induced voltage in rectangular loops. If each part of the lightning conductor is parallel to one of the sides of the loop, the calculation can be reduced to two basic arrangements. Every other arrangement of the loop and the lightning conductor can be constructed by superposing the two basic ones. Accordingly the induced voltage needs to be calculated only in theese cases and the basic components have to be summarised.

articleTitle: A Novel Formula for VHF/UHF Propagation Loss for Land Mobile Communication in Rural Terrain
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The simplified analysis of ground-wave propagation /called "unified analysis"/ in the 2 - 200 MHz frequency band was outlined by Prof. Wojnar and this author at the Third and Fourth Wrocław Symposia. The basic transmission loss /evaluated over the smooth, spherical earth within the adequate distance range/ changes proportionally to the distance raised. to the fourth power. Multiple experiments have shown that this fourth-power-law is valid for frequencies up to approximately 500 ÷ 1000 MHz. It is, however, necessary to introduce corrections allowing for sphericity of earth and for dissipation due to terrain irregularity.

articleTitle: EMC and Communication Satellite Services After WARC-79
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The rapid development of the geostationary satellite orbit produces an increasingly unfavorable EMC environment, giving rise to the widely perceived threat of eventual orbit saturation and denial of access to later entrants. GWARC-79 decided that a Planning Conference for space services should seek to guarantee to all nations equitable future access to the orbit. It is examined which of the space services could be planned and which one of three basic forms of planning might be most appropriate in each case.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Spectrum Monitoring
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report described the Radio Spectrum Measurement System (RSMS) used to measure spectrum usage 1n support of spectrum management functions. The RSMS uses a minicomputer to control the operation of components of the receiving system, Including the antennas, transmission line components, calibration devices and processes, and other related equipment. In addition, the computer performs real-time processing on the measured data to Improve data quality and reduce the cost of data storage. The computer is also used to post process data for particular applications and to produce graphical output tailored to meet to meet a wide range of spectrum management needs. The use of the system for land mobile radio measurements is discussed.

articleTitle: Estimation of Power Absorption and Temperature Rise Within Homan Eye in Presence of Electromagnetic Radiations
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A human eye ball is simulated by prolate spheroidal model and is used in estimating specific time averaged absorbed power density (P), when eye is exposed to 1.5 GHz electromagnetic radiation of 1 mW per square centimeter. Curves for (P) are given for magnetic, electric and cross polarizations. The total time averaged specific absorbed power is further estimated and plotted as a function of frequency using this proposed model. The rise in temperature within the eye is calculated at the point of maximum absorbed power and it depends on the time of exposure of electromagnetic radiations, and its intensity. Results are included.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of a TV-Network
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper, a model of a TV broadcasting system and a method of conducting computer simulation experiments have been described. The model of a TV-network consists of models of network components i.e. transmitter model, antenna model, receiver model, propagation model and topographical and electronic environment models. Simulation experiments may be conducted in order to describe, analize and predict system performance.

articleTitle: Induction in Power Transmission Lines During Geomagnetic Disturbances
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electric field associated with geomagnetic disturbances gives rise to potential differences at the earth's surface. Thus, currents are induced in power transmission lines which are earthed at both ends through transformers. The currents vary so slowly with time that they can be considered direct currents. The phenomenon has been studied in Finland for some years, and in connection with this research induced currents have been measured at four places by recording the current from the transformer neutral into the earth. These measurements are considered in this paper. In addition, theoretical calculation of the potential differences and of the current is discussed.

articleTitle: The Back-to-Front Ratio of a Mirror Antenna with Weak Illumination of the Aperture Edges
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The space selection of the antennae directivity is one of the main parameters in the process of design of the BMC of the various radio systems. To improve the reliability of these systems required is lowering of the side-to-front and back-to-front of the antenna. One probable method for improving of the mirror antenna front-to-back /side/ ratio is the lowering of the illumination value at the aperture edges. Direct using of the geometrical diffraction method in a case of the small /e.g. "zero"/ illumination level at the aperture edges does not give the correct results and solution of this problem is obtained by using the locality principle for the diffraction phenomena. In the neighbourhood of the real radiating feed the additional finite grid is maintained that consists of the isotropic sources. Then the laws for illuminating the grid elements are obtained, for which their directivity patterns and the patterns of the real feed are locally identical in the angle sone, corresponding to the direction onto the mirror edge. finally the equivalent diffraction coefficient for the sources grid is computated. By this method an equation for the mirror antenna back/side/-to-front ratios are derived taking into account the directivity pattern form of the feed. Back-to-front ratio depends from the illumination value at the mirror edges and from the directivity pattern form.

articleTitle: Circuit Properties of Cage Antennae
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: <sup>1</sup>Technical University of Wrocław, Wybrzeże Wyspiańskiego 27, 50-370 Wrocław, Poland. A method of calculations of MF transmitting cage antenna circuit properties is presented. Included are exemplary results of quarter-ware and double-half-wave antenna impedance calculations with allowances made for utilization of correction elements forming a part of the antenna and the influence of parasitic capacitances affixed to the cages.

articleTitle: Observed Radiation Pulses from Lightning and the Localization of Thunderstorms in Sweden
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to evaluate or to improve the performance of electronic systems under the conditions of close lightning a basic knowledge of the properties of thunderstorms and lightning discharges in the time domain and in space is required. A brief description of methods applied and some results obtained in Sweden are given.

articleTitle: Impacts of Solar and Auroral Storms on Power Line Systems
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Geo-electromagnetic activity gives rise to electric potential differences between different points on the earth's surface (earth surface potentials) which cause extraneous quasi DC currents to enter electric power transmission systems through their grounding points. These geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) which may exceed 100 A can cause half-cycle saturation of magnetic devices such as power and current transformers, seriously shortening their operational life-times, and GICs can also cause misoperation of protective devices such as relays and circuit breakers, thus resulting in systems shutdown. Similar systems deteriorating effects are also observed on long metallic grounded pipe lines particularly if extending into sub-auroral and auroral regions. It has also been observed that due to transformer core saturation power line harmonics radiation (PLHR) is created which increases during periods of increased geo-electromagnetic activity. This VLF radiation may cause electromagnetic systems interference (ESI) with neighbouring or earth-satellite communications links, and it may also interact with the magnetosphere and affect chorus activity and electron slot precipitation. The after-effects of these magnetospheric activities 1111y subsequently propagate from the ionosphere through the mesosphere and modulate weather, particularly thunderstorm activity which then may lead to a closed cycle of disturbing events affecting both natural and man-made systems.

articleTitle: Introductory Remarks: From the Scientific Program Committee Chairman
publicationTitle: Fifth International Wroclaw Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is a source of great satisfaction to me, as program chairman of an international symposium, that more than 120 abstracts arrived, most of them of reasonable to good quality, even if many of then did not moot the original dead-line. Ono hopes that those who sent in an accepted abstract, can also be welcomed to the opening session of the Symposium. Large numbers of papers came from the USSR and the organising country, Poland, but the research of many other countries such as USA, Hungary, Italy, Germany F.R., Germany D.R., France, Japan, UK and Yugoslavia is also represented in the papers offered.
